2. SERVICE HOURS AND OFFICE OPERATIONS

2.1 The ASO main office is open to students, families, and staff during the published service hours for the current school year. These hours are posted at the office entrance, on the district website, and in the annual parent handbook.

2.2 Per the ASO manual, the office service hours are 07:30-16:30, Monday through Friday, during the regular academic year. These hours are effective for the current school year and are reviewed annually.

2.3 The office will be closed on all district holidays, during scheduled building closures, and for staff professional development days as designated by the district calendar.

2.4 When the main office is closed, a voicemail message will direct callers to the district's general information line for urgent matters. The ASO Coordinator will check the voicemail and email system at the start of the next business day.

2.5 Walk-in service is available during service hours. Appointments are encouraged for complex matters, including initial intake meetings, triennial reviews, and mediation or dispute resolution conferences.

2.6 Staff should ensure that the main office is staffed at all times during service hours. If a staff member must leave the office, they will coordinate coverage with a colleague or the building front desk.

3. STAFF ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 ASO Coordinator
The ASO Coordinator is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the office, including:
- Oversight of day-to-day operations and compliance with this manual.
- Supervision and evaluation of ASO staff.
- Coordination of Section 504 evaluation and accommodation plan processes.
- Serving as the district liaison for accessibility-related concerns.
- Managing the office budget and resource allocation.
- Reviewing and updating this manual as needed.

- Greeting visitors and answering incoming calls.

- Processing correspondence and maintaining office supplies.
- Assisting with data entry and record keeping.

Section 6: Request and Intake Procedures

6.1 Types of Requests
The ASO receives requests for accessibility services from a variety of sources, including:
- Parents or guardians of students with disabilities.
- School administrators and teachers.
- District departments, such as Transportation, Facilities, and Technology.
- External agencies and advocacy organizations.
- Students themselves (when appropriate).

Requests may include, but are not limited to:
- Section 504 evaluations and accommodation plan development.
- Interpreter services for deaf and hard-of-hearing students.
- Assistive technology assessments and implementation.
- Physical accessibility modifications to school facilities.
- Training for school staff on accessibility topics.

6.2 Intake and Documentation
All requests must be documented using the appropriate intake form. The Administrative Assistant is responsible for logging requests in the ASO tracking system and assigning a case number. The following information must be captured for each request:
- Date of request and method of submission (phone, email, written, or in-person).
- Name and contact information of the person making the request.
- Student name, school, and grade (if applicable).
- Description of the requested service or accommodation.
- Any relevant deadlines or urgent circumstances.

The intake form is the official record of the request and must be completed accurately. Incomplete forms will be returned to the requester for clarification.
The IRF must be completed legibly and in its entirety. The following information is required:

- Date and time of the incident.
- Location of the incident, including building and room number or specific area.
- Name(s) of the individual(s) involved, including student name and school when applicable.
- Name(s) of any witnesses.
- Description of the incident, written in a factual and objective manner. Staff should avoid speculation, opinions, or judgments about the individuals involved.
- Description of any injuries sustained, including the part of the body affected and the apparent severity.
- Actions taken immediately following the incident, such as first aid administered, notification of parents or guardians, or contact with emergency services.
- Name and signature of the person completing the form.
- Date the form was completed.

If any field is not applicable, staff should write "N/A" rather than leaving the field blank. Incomplete forms will be returned to the staff member for correction and may delay the review process.

7.4 Submission and Routing

Completed IRFs must be submitted to the ASO Administrative Assistant within one business day of the incident. The Administrative Assistant will log the form in the incident tracking spreadsheet and assign an incident number. The original form is retained in the ASO office, and copies are distributed as follows:

- One copy to the Director of Accessibility Services.
- One copy to the school principal, if the incident occurred at a school site.
- One copy to the district Risk Management Office, for incidents involving injury or property damage.

For incidents involving a student with a Section 504 plan or an Individualized Education Program (IEP), a copy of the IRF should also be placed in the student's confidential file. Staff should note on the form whether the student has a current plan.

7.5 Follow-Up and Review

The Director of Accessibility Services, or designee, will review each IRF within five business days of submission. The review will determine whether additional follow-up is needed, including:

- Contact with the family or guardian.
- Referral to the district's Risk Management Office.
- Modification of the student's accommodation plan.
- Changes to procedures or equipment to prevent recurrence.
- Additional training for staff.

The outcome of the review will be documented in writing and attached to the original IRF. Staff who submitted the form will be notified of any actions taken that affect their work assignments or responsibilities.

7.6 Confidentiality and Records Retention

All incident reports are confidential student records when they involve a student, and access is limited to staff with a legitimate educational interest. Staff must not discuss incident details with individuals outside of the appropriate chain of command, and must not share copies of IRFs without authorization.

7.7 Reporting to External Agencies

Certain incidents may require reporting to external agencies, including:

- Suspected abuse or neglect, which must be reported to the appropriate child protective services agency in accordance with state law.
- Incidents involving serious injury or death, which must be reported to the district's Risk Management Office immediately.
- Incidents involving the use of restraint or seclusion, which are subject to additional reporting requirements as defined by district policy.
8.0 General Office Operations

8.1 Office Hours and Coverage

The Accessibility Services Office (ASO) maintains regular office hours from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, during the instructional calendar. During school breaks and summer session, hours may be adjusted by the Director and will be posted on the office door and website no fewer than five business days in advance.

The front desk will be staffed at all times during regular office hours. When a staff member is unable to report to work or will be more than fifteen minutes late, they must notify the Administrative Assistant by 6:45 a.m. so that coverage can be arranged. If the Administrative Assistant is unavailable, staff should contact the Director of Accessibility Services directly.

Lunch breaks are scheduled so that the front desk remains covered. Staff should coordinate lunch schedules with the Administrative Assistant at the start of each week. No staff member should leave the office during their scheduled shift without checking out with the front desk and indicating their expected return time.

8.2 Telephone and Voicemail

All incoming calls should be answered by the third ring whenever possible. The standard greeting is: "Accessibility Services Office, this is [name]." Staff should speak clearly and identify themselves by first and last name. When transferring a call, staff should provide the caller with the name and extension of the person receiving the transfer before completing the connection.

Voicemail greetings should be updated at the start of each semester and whenever the staff member will be out of the office for more than one business day. The greeting must include the staff member's name, the fact that they are unavailable, and an alternative contact, either the front desk or a named colleague. Voicemail should be checked at minimum twice daily, once in the morning and once in the afternoon. Messages should be returned within one business day, except during periods of approved leave.

When a caller is distressed or reports an urgent safety concern, staff should not attempt to resolve the matter over the phone alone. Staff should gather the caller's name and contact information, take note of the concern, and inform the caller that the appropriate staff member will follow up. If the concern involves imminent danger to a student or staff member, the caller should be directed to call 911 or the school site administrator immediately, and the ASO staff member should document the call and notify the Director.

8.3 Walk-In Visitors and Appointments

Walk-in visitors are welcome during regular office hours. Staff should greet visitors promptly and determine the purpose of their visit. If the visitor needs to meet with a specific staff member who is unavailable, staff should offer to schedule an appointment or take a message. Visitors should not be left unattended in the office for extended periods.

Appointments with ASO staff should be scheduled through the front desk. Staff are expected to keep their appointment calendars current and to block out times when they are unavailable. When a staff member must cancel an appointment, they should notify the front desk as soon as possible so that the visitor can be contacted and rescheduled. No-show appointments should be documented in the office log and the staff member should attempt to contact the visitor within two business days.

8.4 Mail and Deliveries
9.1 Mail Handling

Incoming mail is delivered to the front desk each weekday by the district courier, usually between 9:00 and 10:00 a.m. A staff member should sort incoming mail the same day it arrives. Items addressed to a specific staff member should be placed in that person's mailbox or on their desk. Items addressed to the office generally, or items without a clear recipient, should be opened by the front desk staff and routed to the appropriate person or program.

Confidential mail, including documents containing student records or medical information, must not be left in open mailboxes or on shared desks. Confidential items should be placed in a sealed envelope and either handed directly to the recipient or placed in the locked file cabinet designated for confidential mail. The front desk staff should maintain a log of confidential mail received, noting the date, sender, recipient, and a brief description of the item. The log should be reviewed quarterly by the Office Manager.

Outgoing mail should be prepared and placed in the outgoing mail basket by 3:00 p.m. to ensure pickup the same day. Certified mail, registered mail, and packages requiring a signature must be brought to the district mailroom by a staff member or the courier must be notified. Postage for ASO correspondence is provided through the district mailroom; staff should not purchase postage with personal funds and seek reimbursement.

9.2 Office Supply and Equipment Requests

Staff may request office supplies through the standard district procurement system. Supply requests should be submitted by the end of the month and are typically filled within two weeks. The Office Manager reviews supply orders and approves requests that fall within the office budget. Requests that exceed the monthly allocation or that are not standard office supplies require the approval of the Director.

Equipment requests, including assistive technology devices, adaptive keyboards, ergonomic furniture, and other accommodations-related equipment, should be submitted in writing to the Director. The request should include a description of the item, the intended use, the student or staff member who will benefit, and any supporting documentation such as a prescription, evaluation report, or recommendation from a specialist. The Director will review the request and respond within ten business days.

Equipment that is received should be inventoried by the Office Manager. Each item should be tagged with a district asset number and recorded in the equipment log. Staff are responsible for the care of equipment assigned to them. Equipment that is damaged, lost, or stolen should be reported to the Office Manager immediately.

9.3 Use of Office Vehicles

The ASO maintains two office vehicles for staff travel to school sites and off-site meetings. Vehicles are reserved through the front desk. Staff should submit a vehicle request at least two business days in advance, indicating the date, time, destination, and purpose of the trip. Same-day requests may be accommodated if a vehicle is available and the request is approved by the Office Manager.

Staff who drive office vehicles must hold a valid driver's license and have completed the district's defensive driving course. A copy of the driver's license should be on file with the Office Manager. Staff should inspect the vehicle before and after each trip, noting any damage or mechanical issues in the vehicle log. Vehicles should be returned with a full tank of gas. Fuel purchases should be made using the district fuel card and receipts should be submitted to the Office Manager.

2. SERVICE HOURS AND OFFICE OPERATIONS

2.1 The ASO main office is open to students, families, and staff during the published service hours for the current school year. These hours are posted at the office entrance, on the district website, and in the annual parent handbook.

2.2 Per the ASO manual, the office service hours are 07:30-16:30, Monday through Friday, during the regular academic year. These hours are effective for the current school year and are reviewed annually.

2.3 The office will be closed on all district holidays, during scheduled building closures, and for staff professional development days as designated by the district calendar.

2.4 When the main office is closed, a voicemail message will direct callers to the district's general information line for urgent matters. The ASO Coordinator will check the voicemail and email system at the start of the next business day.

2.5 Walk-in service is available during service hours. Appointments are encouraged for complex matters, including initial intake meetings, triennial reviews, and mediation or dispute resolution conferences.

2.6 Staff should ensure that the main office is staffed at all times during service hours. If a staff member must leave the office, they will coordinate coverage with a colleague or the building front desk.

Per the ASO manual, the office service_hours are 07:30-16:30. Record status: current.

3. STAFF ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

3.1 ASO Coordinator
The ASO Coordinator is responsible for the overall management and supervision of the office, including:
- Oversight of day-to-day operations and compliance with this manual.
- Supervision and evaluation of ASO staff.
- Coordination of Section 504 evaluation and accommodation plan processes.
- Serving as the district liaison for accessibility-related concerns.
- Managing the office budget and resource allocation.
- Reviewing and updating this manual as needed.

3.2 Administrative Assistant
The Administrative Assistant is the first point of contact for the office and is responsible for:
- Greeting visitors and answering incoming calls.
- Scheduling appointments and maintaining the office calendar.
- Managing intake paperwork and maintaining student files.
- Processing correspondence and maintaining office supplies.
- Assisting with data entry and record keeping.

3.3 Accessibility Specialist (Two Positions)
Accessibility Specialists provide direct support for the implementation of accommodations and accessibility features. Their responsibilities include:
- Conducting classroom observations and environmental assessments.
- Coordinating with building staff on assistive technology and physical access issues.
- Training staff on accommodation implementation.
- Monitoring the effectiveness of accommodations and recommending adjustments.

3.4 Interpreter Services Coordinator
The Interpreter Services Coordinator manages the scheduling and assignment of interpreters for deaf and hard-of-hearing students. Duties include:
- Receiving and processing interpreter requests.
- Coordinating with external interpreter agencies as needed.
- Maintaining a schedule of interpreter assignments.
- Ensuring that interpreters meet district qualifications and confidentiality requirements.

3.5 All staff are expected to maintain a professional and welcoming demeanor. Confidentiality is of the utmost importance, and all staff must complete annual training on the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and district confidentiality policies.

Section 6: Request and Intake Procedures

6.1 Types of Requests
The ASO receives requests for accessibility services from a variety of sources, including:
- Parents or guardians of students with disabilities.
- School administrators and teachers.
- District departments, such as Transportation, Facilities, and Technology.
- External agencies and advocacy organizations.
- Students themselves (when appropriate).

Requests may include, but are not limited to:
- Section 504 evaluations and accommodation plan development.
- Interpreter services for deaf and hard-of-hearing students.
- Assistive technology assessments and implementation.
- Physical accessibility modifications to school facilities.
- Training for school staff on accessibility topics.

6.2 Intake and Documentation
All requests must be documented using the appropriate intake form. The Administrative Assistant is responsible for logging requests in the ASO tracking system and assigning a case number. The following information must be captured for each request:
- Date of request and method of submission (phone, email, written, or in-person).
- Name and contact information of the person making the request.
- Student name, school, and grade (if applicable).
- Description of the requested service or accommodation.
- Any relevant deadlines or urgent circumstances.

The intake form is the official record of the request and must be completed accurately. Incomplete forms will be returned to the requester for clarification.

The IRF must be completed legibly and in its entirety. The following information is required:

- Date and time of the incident.
- Location of the incident, including building and room number or specific area.
- Name(s) of the individual(s) involved, including student name and school when applicable.
- Name(s) of any witnesses.
- Description of the incident, written in a factual and objective manner. Staff should avoid speculation, opinions, or judgments about the individuals involved.
- Description of any injuries sustained, including the part of the body affected and the apparent severity.
- Actions taken immediately following the incident, such as first aid administered, notification of parents or guardians, or contact with emergency services.
- Name and signature of the person completing the form.
- Date the form was completed.

If any field is not applicable, staff should write "N/A" rather than leaving the field blank. Incomplete forms will be returned to the staff member for correction and may delay the review process.

7.4 Submission and Routing

Completed IRFs must be submitted to the ASO Administrative Assistant within one business day of the incident. The Administrative Assistant will log the form in the incident tracking spreadsheet and assign an incident number. The original form is retained in the ASO office, and copies are distributed as follows:

- One copy to the Director of Accessibility Services.
- One copy to the school principal, if the incident occurred at a school site.
- One copy to the district Risk Management Office, for incidents involving injury or property damage.

For incidents involving a student with a Section 504 plan or an Individualized Education Program (IEP), a copy of the IRF should also be placed in the student's confidential file. Staff should note on the form whether the student has a current plan.

7.5 Follow-Up and Review

The Director of Accessibility Services, or designee, will review each IRF within five business days of submission. The review will determine whether additional follow-up is needed, including:

- Contact with the family or guardian.
- Referral to the district's Risk Management Office.
- Modification of the student's accommodation plan.
- Changes to procedures or equipment to prevent recurrence.
- Additional training for staff.

The outcome of the review will be documented in writing and attached to the original IRF. Staff who submitted the form will be notified of any actions taken that affect their work assignments or responsibilities.

7.6 Confidentiality and Records Retention

All incident reports are confidential student records when they involve a student, and access is limited to staff with a legitimate educational interest. Staff must not discuss incident details with individuals outside of the appropriate chain of command, and must not share copies of IRFs without authorization.

7.7 Reporting to External Agencies

Certain incidents may require reporting to external agencies, including:

- Suspected abuse or neglect, which must be reported to the appropriate child protective services agency in accordance with state law.
- Incidents involving serious injury or death, which must be reported to the district's Risk Management Office immediately.

documents.content:
8.0 General Office Operations

8.1 Office Hours and Coverage

The Accessibility Services Office (ASO) maintains regular office hours from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, during the instructional calendar. During school breaks and summer session, hours may be adjusted by the Director and will be posted on the office door and website no fewer than five business days in advance.

The front desk will be staffed at all times during regular office hours. When a staff member is unable to report to work or will be more than fifteen minutes late, they must notify the Administrative Assistant by 6:45 a.m. so that coverage can be arranged. If the Administrative Assistant is unavailable, staff should contact the Director of Accessibility Services directly.

Lunch breaks are scheduled so that the front desk remains covered. Staff should coordinate lunch schedules with the Administrative Assistant at the start of each week. No staff member should leave the office during their scheduled shift without checking out with the front desk and indicating their expected return time.

8.2 Telephone and Voicemail

All incoming calls should be answered by the third ring whenever possible. The standard greeting is: "Accessibility Services Office, this is [name]." Staff should speak clearly and identify themselves by first and last name. When transferring a call, staff should provide the caller with the name and extension of the person receiving the transfer before completing the connection.

Voicemail greetings should be updated at the start of each semester and whenever the staff member will be out of the office for more than one business day. The greeting must include the staff member's name, the fact that they are unavailable, and an alternative contact, either the front desk or a named colleague. Voicemail should be checked at minimum twice daily, once in the morning and once in the afternoon. Messages should be returned within one business day, except during periods of approved leave.

When a caller is distressed or reports an urgent safety concern, staff should not attempt to resolve the matter over the phone alone. Staff should gather the caller's name and contact information, take note of the concern, and inform the caller that the appropriate staff member will follow up. If the concern involves imminent danger to a student or staff member, the caller should be directed to call 911 or the school site administrator immediately, and the ASO staff member should document the call and notify the Director.

8.3 Walk-In Visitors and Appointments

Walk-in visitors are welcome during regular office hours. Staff should greet visitors promptly and determine the purpose of their visit. If the visitor needs to meet with a specific staff member who is unavailable, staff should offer to schedule an appointment or take a message. Visitors should not be left unattended in the office for extended periods.

Appointments with ASO staff should be scheduled through the front desk. Staff are expected to keep their appointment calendars current and to block out times when they are unavailable. When a staff member must cancel an appointment, they should notify the front desk as soon as possible so that the visitor can be contacted and rescheduled. No-show appointments should be documented in the office log and the staff member should attempt to contact the visitor within two business days.

8.4 Mail and Deliveries

documents.title: Accessibility Services Office Policy and Procedure Manual
documents.content:
9.1 Mail Handling

Incoming mail is delivered to the front desk each weekday by the district courier, usually between 9:00 and 10:00 a.m. A staff member should sort incoming mail the same day it arrives. Items addressed to a specific staff member should be placed in that person's mailbox or on their desk. Items addressed to the office generally, or items without a clear recipient, should be opened by the front desk staff and routed to the appropriate person or program.

Confidential mail, including documents containing student records or medical information, must not be left in open mailboxes or on shared desks. Confidential items should be placed in a sealed envelope and either handed directly to the recipient or placed in the locked file cabinet designated for confidential mail. The front desk staff should maintain a log of confidential mail received, noting the date, sender, recipient, and a brief description of the item. The log should be reviewed quarterly by the Office Manager.

Outgoing mail should be prepared and placed in the outgoing mail basket by 3:00 p.m. to ensure pickup the same day. Certified mail, registered mail, and packages requiring a signature must be brought to the district mailroom by a staff member or the courier must be notified. Postage for ASO correspondence is provided through the district mailroom; staff should not purchase postage with personal funds and seek reimbursement.

9.2 Office Supply and Equipment Requests

Staff may request office supplies through the standard district procurement system. Supply requests should be submitted by the end of the month and are typically filled within two weeks. The Office Manager reviews supply orders and approves requests that fall within the office budget. Requests that exceed the monthly allocation or that are not standard office supplies require the approval of the Director.

Equipment requests, including assistive technology devices, adaptive keyboards, ergonomic furniture, and other accommodations-related equipment, should be submitted in writing to the Director. The request should include a description of the item, the intended use, the student or staff member who will benefit, and any supporting documentation such as a prescription, evaluation report, or recommendation from a specialist. The Director will review the request and respond within ten business days.

Equipment that is received should be inventoried by the Office Manager. Each item should be tagged with a district asset number and recorded in the equipment log. Staff are responsible for the care of equipment assigned to them. Equipment that is damaged, lost, or stolen should be reported to the Office Manager immediately.

9.3 Use of Office Vehicles

The ASO maintains two office vehicles for staff travel to school sites and off-site meetings. Vehicles are reserved through the front desk. Staff should submit a vehicle request at least two business days in advance, indicating the date, time, destination, and purpose of the trip. Same-day requests may be accommodated if a vehicle is available and the request is approved by the Office Manager.

Staff who drive office vehicles must hold a valid driver's license and have completed the district's defensive driving course. A copy of the driver's license should be on file with the Office Manager. Staff should inspect the vehicle before and after each trip, noting any damage or mechanical issues in the vehicle log. Vehicles should be returned with a full tank of gas. Fuel purchases should be made using the district fuel card and receipts should be submitted to the Office Manager.
